findings.title: Emails are sent with the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered request list. Any email that was dropped as an existing attendee still matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. That existing attendee then gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a new-booking email) instead of the 'guests added' notification. The newly created guests are the ones that should be passed, i.e. `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses `&&`, so admins are denied
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` only passes for owners. `isTeamAdmin` is true for ADMIN or OWNER and `isTeamOwner` is true only for OWNER, so the `&&` excludes plain team admins. It should be `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`. As written, team admins who are neither organizer nor attendee get FORBIDDEN even though the variable name says admin-or-owner is allowed.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The handler allows attendees and team admins to call it, but it builds the `EventManager` from `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `...user`). The calendar events being updated belong to the booking organizer (`booking.user`). When the caller is an attendee or admin, the manager holds the wrong user's credentials and destination calendar. The organizer's calendar event is then not updated, or the update fails. In that case the guests are saved in the DB but never added to the calendar event. The organizer's credentials/destination calendar should be used.

findings.title: DB is mutated before the calendar update, with no failure handling
findings.body: Attendees are written to the DB (lines 92-106) before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and that call is not wrapped in try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails and the user sees an error. The guests are already persisted as attendees and no notification emails go out. A retry then hits the 'existing attendee' filter and fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, leaving the booking in an inconsistent state.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive; no server-side dedupe or limit
findings.body: The blacklist is lower-cased, but `guest` is compared as-is (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The same applies to the existing-attendee check (`guest === attendee.email`), so case variants of an existing attendee are inserted as duplicates. The server also never dedupes the input list. The uniqueness rule lives only in the client dialog, so a direct tRPC call with repeated emails creates duplicate attendee rows. Neither the schema nor the handler caps the array length. Any attendee can submit an arbitrarily large list, which triggers one email per guest plus extra emails to every attendee.

findings.title: No check on booking status or end time before adding guests
findings.body: The UI only offers the action for confirmed bookings, but the handler enforces nothing. A caller can add guests to a cancelled, rejected, pending or already-ended booking via the API. That writes attendees, pushes calendar updates, and sends 'guests added' / 'scheduled' emails for a booking that no longer exists. The handler should reject non-ACCEPTED bookings and bookings in the past.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `disableStandardEmails` settings and never emails team members
findings.body: Every other email sender takes `eventTypeMetadata` and honors `disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee`. This one does not, so event types that disabled standard emails still get these emails. In addition, `addGuests.handler.ts` builds `evt` without a `team` field, so the `calendarEvent.team?.members` loop never runs and team hosts are never notified.

findings.title: New guests are created with an empty name and the organizer's locale
findings.body: Guests are stored with `name: ""` and the organizer's `locale`/`timeZone`. The email templates then render ` <email>` recipients and empty-name greetings, and the guest receives emails in the organizer's language rather than their own.

findings.title: Validation error and form state not reset reliably; error fallback unreachable
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation but is never cleared on edit, on successful submit, or when the dialog is closed through the overlay or X (`onOpenChange`). Only the Cancel button resets it, so the red error can show up the next time the dialog opens. The same applies to the email list when the dialog is closed outside Cancel. In `onError`, the string `` `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` `` is always truthy, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is dead code. The user sees an ugly message such as 'BAD_REQUEST: ...', or a raw zod JSON string for validation errors.

findings.title: Hardcoded untranslated tooltip and dangling label association
findings.body: The tooltip text `"Remove email"` is hardcoded English in a component that otherwise uses `t()`, so it will not be localized. The `<label htmlFor="emails">` points to an id that no input has, so the label is not associated with any field.

findings.title: No tests for the new endpoint's authorization, filtering and email behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a new mutation with permission logic (organizer / attendee / team admin), blacklist and duplicate filtering, calendar updates and several email paths, but adds no unit or e2e tests. The bugs above (the `&&` admin check, the wrong `guests` list passed to the emails, case-sensitive filtering) would be caught by even basic handler tests.
